description.en: An event-centric LinkML schema for representing cultural heritage information, aligned with CIDOC-CRM and PROV-O through exact/broad mappings and subproperty bridges, enabling provenance tracking and ritual-spatial-temporal reasoning.

definition.value: An event-centric LinkML schema for representing cultural heritage information, aligned with CIDOC-CRM and PROV-O through exact/broad mappings and subproperty bridges, enabling provenance tracking and ritual-spatial-temporal reasoning.
Religious or philosophical tradition (e.g., Hindu, Buddhist, Syncretic)

Root container for cultural heritage data instances. PLACEMENT RULE: put each instance in the most specific collection available (e.g. a Festival in festivals, not ritual_events; a Person in persons, not actors); broader collections exist for instances of the general classes only.

design_note.value: Serialization construct, not a domain class: this is the LinkML tree_root that anchors JSON/YAML dataset serializations (its collection properties exist for data exchange only). Reasoners and domain queries should ignore it; RDF instance data does not need a Container node.

definition.value: Tantric ritual process of selecting a new Living Goddess from eligible candidates. Involves examination of 32 auspicious physical marks (lakshana), horoscope matching with the city and ruling authority, and tests of fearlessness (e.g., remaining calm among buffalo heads and masked dancers in darkness). Performed by committee of Vajracharya priests, royal priest (Raj Jyotish), and astrologer.

An eligibility criterion a candidate must satisfy to assume the Kumari role. Modelled as explicit subclasses so 'what are the eligibility criteria?' is a subclass query, not free text.

The 'fearlessness test' popularly described (animal heads, masked dancers in darkness). Its historical and contemporary practice is DISPUTED -- some former Kumaris contest how it is described. Represented as an assessment whose accounts are source-attributed via has_assertion, NOT as a mandatory criterion.

scopeNote.value: Deliberately not a SelectionCriterion subclass: popular accounts and lived testimony disagree. Attach each account as a Assertion (CRMinf I2 Belief) with its own source and confidence.

definition.value: A performed assessment carried out during Kumari selection. Modelled as an event (not a hard criterion) so that source-specific, possibly conflicting accounts of whether/how it was conducted attach as provenanced Assertions rather than being asserted as fact.

Hereditary social group (Jati) with specific ritual roles and occupational duties
Direct LinkML representation of prov:Activity. Applied to events and processes that use, transform, generate, document, assess, or verify entities.

Direct LinkML representation of prov:Entity. Applied to physical, digital, conceptual, and assertion-bearing things that participate in provenance relations. PROVENANCE SCOPE (design decision): for classes whose instances are real-world referents (structures, deities, places, actors), the provenance slots (was_derived_from, was_attributed_to, was_generated_by, generated_at_time) describe the DATA RECORD about the referent, not the referent itself -- a stupa is not generated by the survey that records it. Referent-level history is modelled through events (Production, DestructionEvent, etc.). RDF deployments SHOULD carry record-level provenance in named graphs or on InformationObject/Assertion nodes.
Intentional ritual activity that activates sacred space, invokes deities, and binds social groups

A provenance-bearing belief or claim about a heritage entity or event. The assertion is represented as CRMinf I2 Belief and as a prov:Entity, allowing source, attribution, generation time, revision, confidence, and reconciliation status to be recorded explicitly.

design_note.value: RitualType currently mixes three orthogonal axes: worship-frequency (NityaPuja/NaimittikaPuja/KamyaPuja), ritual form (Homa/Jatra/MaskedPerformance), and lifecycle (InstallationRitual/ReturningRitual). Consider splitting into RitualFrequency + RitualForm. Also: Circumambulation/ProcessionalMovement/ProcessionRitual/RelicTour overlap with RitualEvent.route_places/start_place/end_place/route_description -- pick one canonical mechanism for moving rituals.
